draft.title: Point and chromosomal mutations
card: A mutation is a change in the DNA sequence of an organism. Mutations are grouped by how much DNA they change.
a change to one or a few bases in a gene. One base may be swapped for another, added or removed.
a change to part or all of a chromosome. A deletion removes a section of a chromosome. A duplication copies a section so it appears more than once.
A chromosomal mutation can affect many genes at once. A point mutation changes only a tiny stretch of DNA, but this can still change a protein.
draft.remember: Point mutations change a few bases. Chromosomal mutations change a section or all of a chromosome.

a.q: Which change is a chromosomal mutation?
opts: A section of a chromosome is copied twice in a row
One base in a gene is swapped for a different base
A single base is added within a gene
Two bases in a gene are swapped for other bases
a.why: Copying a section of a chromosome so it appears twice is a duplication, which changes part of a chromosome. The other three change only one or a few bases, so they are point mutations. Swapping two bases is tempting, but it is still only a few bases.
a.clue: Look for the change that involves a whole section of a chromosome.

b.q: A child has a condition because a section of one chromosome, holding many genes, is missing. How should this mutation be described?
opts: A chromosomal mutation, because part of a chromosome is lost
A point mutation, because only one gene is mainly affected
A point mutation, because the DNA was removed, not changed
A chromosomal mutation, because it must affect every gene
b.why: Losing a section of a chromosome is a deletion, so it is a chromosomal mutation. Removing DNA does not make it a point mutation: that type changes only one or a few bases. The last option is wrong because a chromosomal mutation can affect many genes, not necessarily every gene.
b.clue: Think about how much DNA is missing, not just that something was removed.

a.best: A section of a chromosome is copied twice in a row

b.best: A chromosomal mutation, because part of a chromosome is lost

problems.detail: Why (b) calls the 'must affect every gene' option 'the last option', but options are shown in random order. As displayed it is the second option, and the last is 'A point mutation, because the DNA was removed, not changed'. The explanation should name the option by its content, not its position.
